Subject: AtlasBio discovery recap & procurement checkpoints

Hi Maya — great conversation today, thanks for walking through the pilot goals. Quick post-call recap and the procurement questions we promised to surface to our AP/finance playbook so you can decide next steps: 

- Pilot scope: 3 internal teams, 1 production endpoint, expected monthly token volume ~2M.
- Preferred timeline: pilot kickoff in September, production roll by Q4 if pilot passes.

Procurement / payment items we flagged:
1) Payment method: do you prefer vendor PO (net-30) or payment by corporate card? Which is easier for AtlasBio to get approved for a pilot?
2) Vendor onboarding: will AP require a vendor packet (W-9, insurance cert, SOC 2 report)?
3) Marketplace option: you mentioned your Platform team sometimes prefers to buy through cloud marketplaces — should we include marketplace enablement as an alternative in the SOW?

Next steps I propose:
- Maya: confirm preferred payment path (PO vs card) and the person on your side who owns POs.
- AtlasBio procurement: if PO, share vendor onboarding checklist or a point of contact so we can expedite.
- Karthik/Vivek: I'll loop you in to scope out SOW language that supports either payment path (and marketplace clause).

Attaching a short AP checklist and a SOW draft outline for reference. Happy to schedule a 30-min procurement intro if that helps.

Thanks —

Date: Tue, 3 Aug 2027 09:08:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: AtlasBio discovery recap & procurement checkpoints

Thanks Soojin — helpful recap. A few clarifications from procurement: 

- For pilots under $25k we typically accept a corporate card or direct invoice; anything above that requires a PO and our vendor onboarding (W-9 + supplier form). Pilot estimate here might land close to the PO threshold depending on token overages.
- We do require SOC 2 Type II evidence for vendors touching production data; for a pilot that's internal-only we can accept SOC 2 Type I or an interim security questionnaire, but need formal confirmation.
- Marketplace purchases are preferred by Platform for longer-term contracts, but marketplace onboarding takes 2–4 weeks and can complicate pilot timing.

Action items on our side:
- I can confirm the PO owner (Amy Li) and intro if we go PO route.
- I attached our supplier intake form to this reply (procurement@atlasbio.com).

Can you confirm whether Redwood can accept a short form security questionnaire and whether the SOW can be split into a capped pilot agreement (to stay under $25k) with an option to expand?

Best,
Maya
Head of Data Products
AtlasBio
maya.singh@atlasbio.com

Attachment: atlasbio_supplier_intake.pdf

From: Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwoodinference.com>
To: Maya Singh <maya.singh@atlasbio.com>, Procurement Team <procurement@atlasbio.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwoodinference.com>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Wed, 4 Aug 2027 11:41:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: AtlasBio discovery recap & procurement checkpoints

Hi Maya — thanks for the clarity. Quick answers: 

- Security: we can provide our SOC 2 Type II report under NDA; for pilot speed we are OK with completing your short security questionnaire (Karthik can own that).
- Pricing/SOW: we can split the engagement into a capped pilot SOW (<= $25k) with an option to convert to an annual production agreement if you choose to expand. That avoids the PO requirement up front if you want to use a card/invoice for the pilot.
- Marketplace: we can enable a marketplace purchase, but timeline is longer. If pilot timing is priority, recommend card or capped invoice to stay in the 2–3 week window.

Next steps: 
1) Maya — if you want to avoid PO delays, confirm whether AtlasBio can use a card or short invoice for the pilot; otherwise please intro Amy Li so we can start vendor onboarding.
2) Karthik — can you take the security questionnaire and prepare a short redacted SOC 2 package we can share under NDA?
3) Vivek — can you draft a capped pilot SOW that includes an option to convert to yearly billing or marketplace path?

I’ll hold a 30-min slot Thu morning for a procurement intro if Amy is available.

Cheers,
Soojin
Enterprise Account Executive
Redwood Inference
